clue.text: Bank of Durham — place to dress a team?

explanation.surface: A riverside in Durham doubles as a dressing room for a football side.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham stands on the River Wear, so its bank is Wearside. Read as two words, WEAR (put on clothes) and SIDE (a team) give a jokey changing room.
explanation.definitionFit: The district along the River Wear is called Wearside; split in two it suggests clothing a sports eleven.

clue.text: Brief counsel

parts.note: brief looks like a lawyer's brief with counsel as the barrister, but it means short guidance in a single utterance

explanation.surface: A barrister given a brief.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal pairing of 'brief' and 'counsel' is the misdirection; read them as short and guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: A short piece of guidance is a tip given in a sentence or so.

clue.text: See 1
Suffering caused by disturbed rest on board

indicators.note: on board means placed aboard, inside the ship letters

parts.note: a ship is boarded, and SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of 'rest' are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Pain caused by a broken night's sleep aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns REST into TRES, put inside SS, the steamship; 'on board' is a common way of saying 'inside SS'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is strain or pressure that causes distress.

clue.text: Lady in goal going straight for the corners

indicators.note: going here means moving about, so the letters of 'Lady in goal' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A female goalkeeper dives straight for the corners of the net.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal line runs straight from one corner to the opposite corner.

clue.text: Resting, the good man has a twitch

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A saintly fellow can't keep still because of a nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless or at rest is described as static.

clue.text: Burlesque attempt to cover an undergarment

indicators.note: covering means the attempt's letters wrap round the others

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a vest is an undergarment, worn under a shirt in British usage

explanation.surface: A comic show tries to hide an item of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque parody, much like a burlesque.

clue.text: Out-and-out though alternatively in

indicators.note: in means one word is put inside the other

parts.note: or is the word for an alternative

explanation.surface: Total, though maybe otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: OR goes inside THOUGH after THO.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough means complete and absolute, as in a thorough rogue.

clue.text: Secret ciphers devised as a protection for fencing, perhaps

indicators.note: devised means the letters are worked into something new

parts.note: a cipher is a zero, nought, written O

explanation.surface: Coded messages were invented to protect a sword fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges SECRET plus OO. 'fencing' is garden fences, not swordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a wood preservative painted onto timber such as garden fences.

clue.text: Several changes following king in defeat

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the king's letter in the answer

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of 'Several' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Several alterations of fortune after a monarch's loss in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges SEVERAL into EVERSAL, which follows R.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a setback or defeat, a turn of fortune for the worse.

clue.text: Familiar lass with seaweed in abundance

parts.note: gal is a colloquial, familiar word for a girl
ore is an old name for seaweed, as in oarweed

explanation.surface: A girl on the beach finds plenty of seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: ORE as seaweed (oarweed, a kelp) is a crossword favourite worth remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore follows its noun and means plentiful, in great quantity.

clue.text: Firm backing new casino at one time

indicators.note: backing turns the firm's abbreviation round so it reads right to left

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: new means the letters of 'casino' come out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A company puts money behind a newly opened gambling house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses CO to OC; 'new' rearranges CASINO into CASION.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a particular instance or moment when something happens.

clue.text: Voices a number of alternatives

parts.note: ten is a number
the word or introduces alternatives, so 'ors' are alternatives

explanation.surface: Singers are offered several choices.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenors are high male singing voices, and the singers who have them.

clue.text: She's apparently more than equal to her spouse

definitions.text: She's apparently more than equal to her spouse

parts.words: She's apparently more than equal to her spouse
parts.note: read literally, a partner who is a superior portion of the couple rather than an equal one

explanation.surface: A wife who outshines her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is affectionately called one's improved partner, literally a superior half of the pair.

clue.text: Drunk from the tap?

parts.note: a whimsical reading: someone tipsy on tap water would be tight on water, a word that really means sealed against leaks

explanation.surface: Someone who got drunk on tap water.
explanation.definitionFit: Watertight means sealed so no liquid gets through, and also, of an argument, without flaws.

clue.text: Got the bullet finally

parts.note: getting the bullet usually means being sacked; here it is taken literally, a fatal gunshot

explanation.surface: At last someone was fired from their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got the bullet' suggests getting the sack; literally, a bullet that kills.
explanation.definitionFit: Killed by gunfire is the plain meaning, a person fatally hit.

clue.text: Symbolic tale Ella brought up, ending in bloodshed

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gory means bloody, full of bloodshed

explanation.surface: Ella raised a story with a bloody finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses ELLA to ALLE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story whose characters and events stand for deeper meanings.

clue.text: Part of the programme, one concludes

definitions.text: Part of the programme, one concludes

parts.words: Part of the programme, one concludes
parts.note: the closing section of a play or broadcast, the bit that wraps things up

explanation.surface: A section of a show that one infers.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is a closing speech or section at the end of a play or broadcast.

clue.text: Rising hovercraft navigators

parts.note: a helicopter rises and hovers, so those steering it are cryptically pilots of a craft that hovers

explanation.surface: People steering hovercraft lift off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hovercraft' looks like the sea-skimming vehicle; here it means any craft that hovers, a helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: Helicopter flyers rise vertically and hover, so they are steerers of a hovering aircraft.

clue.text: Police dog informer

explanation.surface: A canine that tips off the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a hound used in sniffing work, and old slang for a spy or informer.

clue.text: Fish pie in duplicate?

indicators.note: in means the pie goes inside the fish

parts.note: a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Two of the same fish pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Copied means duplicated, reproduced as a second version.

clue.text: Stoned around a foreign port

indicators.note: around means the letters of 'Stoned' are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone high wanders about an overseas harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a ferry port on the Belgian coast.

clue.text: The beverage found near Reading

parts.note: ale is a beverage, a beer

explanation.surface: A drink discovered close to some reading matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town in Berkshire, England, not something you read; Theale is a village just west of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Theale is a Berkshire village a few miles from the town of Reading.

clue.text: Distressing to discover four grouse shot to pieces

indicators.note: a bird shot to pieces is broken up, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: It is upsetting to find four game birds blasted apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot to pieces' mixes IV with GROUSE to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grievous means causing serious grief or suffering, as in grievous harm.

clue.text: No huge meal, but as much as need be

indicators.note: meal is grain ground up, so the letters of 'No huge' are ground into a new order

explanation.surface: Not a giant dinner, yet it satisfies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meal' looks like food but signals the anagram, in the sense of ground grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sufficient is all that is required, no more.

clue.text: Confident colour

explanation.surface: Sure of oneself, and the hue to prove it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine means optimistic and assured, and also blood-red, a heraldic and artists' colour.

clue.text: Poet with a thirst to study

parts.note: someone thirsty is dry
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A thirsty writer of verse retreats to his study.
explanation.walkthrough: John Dryden was a 17th-century English poet laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was an English poet and playwright, Poet Laureate from 1668.

clue.text: Upset by a push on the diving-board, perhaps

definitions.text: a push on the diving-board, perhaps

explanation.surface: A diver is shoved off the board and takes offence.
explanation.walkthrough: A push sends a diver OFF the END of the board, so OFF-ENDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Offended means hurt or upset; read as off-ended it describes being sent off the end of a board.
